note: Every site in src/ where text could be compared, cased, ordered or cut into words by something other than Unicode: toLowerCase/toUpperCase/toLocale*Case, localeCompare, Intl.Collator, normalize, SQL COLLATE NOCASE, LOWER(, UPPER(, GLOB (any case) and LIKE (capitals), and in regular expressions \b, \B, \w, \W, ASCII letter classes and the i flag on a RegExp built from data. And every English word the code matches text against: a regex holding a word (re-word) or a letter beside an anchor (re-affix), a word compared (str-eq, str-case), searched or cut on (str-includes, str-startsWith, str-split and the like), listed (str-list, str-alt, str-split-list) or used as a key read by a computed key (str-key); a site the type checker types as a string-literal union is a fixed choice and needs no entry. scripts/test-text-comparisons.mjs holds each file's sites, per pattern, to these counts. What a thing is (an item's kind, a check's circumstance, a save's cause) comes from a field, never from English words in text written in the table's language; the table-language entries are the readers that still do, listed to be replaced, and the english-extra entries the English words kept beside a reading that serves every language, each with why a miss costs nothing more. Text a person writes (story, player, author, homebrew and workshop text, and searches) goes through the helpers in src/lib/language/text-logic.ts (textKey, words, containsPhrase, namesPattern, findNamed, compareNames, slugOf, asciiSlugOf), and stemmerWords in ./language.ts; a site classed human may stand only in the files under "humanTextIn". A new site is either one of those helpers or classified here with the reason it stays.

classes.human: text a person writes, compared only where "humanTextIn" allows
classes.key: ids, fixed choices, codes, paths, headers, protocol tokens and the engine's own vocabulary
classes.display: an initial or a label's case, shown, never compared
classes.english-extra: English words read in table text as an extra beside a reading that serves every language, each listed with why a miss costs no more than a table in another language already pays
classes.english-source: English the code matches text against that is itself English by source: SRD, content-pack and stat-block text, ODM's own rows, prompts and formats, the English names of the reference rows
classes.table-language: English words read in text written in the table's language (the model's prose, a player's words, an author's free text): listed reader by reader until a structured field replaces it, never added to
